subject.title: Feature: Add denylist support for exec-approvals

question: Should native exec deny patterns be an additive human-approval override across all permissive modes, and must gateway and node hosts provide identical prompt-versus-deny behavior for every supported configuration source?
rationale: Current main has no such policy, external plugins do not own built-in host enforcement, and the open candidate necessarily chooses security precedence, durable-trust, fallback, and cross-host semantics that automation cannot authorize.

options.title: Approve additive approval override
options.body: Treat every deny-pattern hit as human-only approval before broad allow or durable trust, require documented gateway/node parity for supported configuration sources, and land the linked candidate after proof.

options.title: Allow fail-closed host asymmetry
options.body: Accept the linked design with documented cases where node-local-only rules hard-deny because the gateway cannot prepare a prompt.

options.title: Reject native deny patterns
options.body: Keep core on allowlist and strict modes and direct advanced deny policies to external policy plugins, acknowledging they do not replace all built-in host enforcement paths.

recommendation.title: Approve additive approval override
recommendation.body: Treat every deny-pattern hit as human-only approval before broad allow or durable trust, require documented gateway/node parity for supported configuration sources, and land the linked candidate after proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the deepest recent history on exec approval semantics and is already the discussion's likely follow-up owner.
